final_answer:
>>> The sunk cost fallacy refers to the tendency to continue investing time, money, or resources into a project or decision based on the cumulative investment already made, even when it is no longer rational or beneficial to do so.  
>>> In the business domain, a company might continue funding a failing product line simply because they have already invested millions into its development, ignoring the fact that the product is unlikely to succeed in the market.  
>>> In personal relationships, someone might stay in an unhappy marriage or partnership because they have invested years of time and effort, even though it is clear that the relationship is not fulfilling or healthy.  
>>> In education, a student might persist in pursuing a degree in a field they dislike simply because they have already spent a significant amount of time and money on it, rather than switching to a more suitable major.
